questions.q_en: A wheel makes 700 revolutions to cover a distance of 77 kilometres. What will be the diameter of the wheel?
questions.solution_en:
Distance covered by wheel in 1 revolution = π*diameter

Therefore distance covered in 700 revolutions = 700* π*diameter

According to question, 700* π*diameter = 77*1000

Diameter = 77*1000*7/(22*700) = 35 m

Hence, the diameter of wheel is 35 m.

questions.q_en: The perimeter of a triangle is 30 cm and its area is numerically equal to the sum of its sides. If one of the sides measures 12 cm, what is the length (in cm) of the largest side of the triangle?
questions.solution_en:
Let the largest side of the triangle be x cm.

Given, one of the sides = 12 cm.

∴ The remaining two sides are x cm and (18 - x) cm.

Given, area of the triangle = perimeter

=> √{15(15 - 12)(15 - x)(15 - 18 + x)} = 30 [According to Heron's formula]

=> 15 * 3 * (15 - x) (x - 3) = 30 * 30

=> (15 - x)(x - 3) = 20

=> 15x - 45 - x² + 3x = 20

=> x² - 18x + 65 = 0

=> (x - 13)(x - 5) = 0

=> x = 13 cm (largest side of the triangle).

questions.q_en: If area of circle is halved when its radius is decreased by n then what will be the radius of the circle?
questions.solution_en:
Let us suppose radius of the circle be R.

Hence according to the question, (pR2/p(R-n)2) = 2/1

=> R2/(R-n)2 = 2/1

=> √2 (R-n) = R

=> √2R - R = √2n

=> R(√2-1) = √2n

=> R = √2n/(√2-1)

From a circular sheet of area 1386 cm2, 2 cm wide five circular rings of variable radius were cut. What percentage of the sheet remained?
questions.solution_en:
As we know, area of circle = πr2, where 'r' is the radius of the circle

=> Radius of sheet = √[(1386 X 7)/22] = √441 = 21 cm

=> Radius of remaining sheet = 21 - 5(2) = 11 cm

Area of remaining sheet = (22/7) X 11 X 11 = 380.3 cm2

= 576√3 cm2

questions.q_en: Two sides of a triangular field are 25 meters and 17 meters respectively and its perimeter is 54 meters. Find the area of the field.
questions.solution_en:
Perimeter =sum of 3 sides of the field.

So third side of the triangle field= 54-(25+17) =12 meter

S =(25+17+12)/2=27

Area of the triangle field =square root of (27*(27-25)*(27-17)(27-12))

Area = square root of (27*2*10*15)

Hence Area of the triangle field =90 square meter

questions.q_en: The area of a circular field is 9856 cm2. If a person crosses the field along the diameter, calculate the distance that he will travel (in cm).
questions.solution_en:
πr2 = 9856

=> (22/7) r2=9856

=> r2=9856*7/22

=> r= 56

So, the distance that he has to travel = 2*56 = 112 cm

questions.q_en: Perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 36 cm and perimeter of circle is 220 cm. Find the difference between side of triangle and radius of circle. (use π = 22/7)
questions.solution_en:
Perimeter of equilateral triangle

Side of triangle = 36/3 = 12 cm

Perimeter of circle = 2 πr

According to question,

2 πr = 220

2 * 22/7 * r = 220

r = 220 * 7/(22 * 2)

r = 35 cm

Required difference = 35 - 12 = 23 cm

questions.q_en: Maximum value of circumference of a circle inscribed in a square is 176 cm. What is the difference between area of circle and area of square? (take π = 22/7)
questions.solution_en:
Circumference of circle = 2 * (22/7) * radius = 176

Radius = 28 cm

Then, side of square = 2 * 28 = 56 cm

Then, area of square = 56 * 56 = 3136

Area of circle = (22/7) * 28 * 28 = 2464

Therefore, difference = 3136 - 2464 = 672 cm2

questions.q_en: A person started running around a circular track of radius 21 meters with speed of 39.6 km/h. Find the time taken to finish one complete round of the track.
questions.solution_en:
Total running length = 2πr = 2 * (22/7) * 21

Speed = 39.6 km/h = 39.6 * (5/18) = 11 m/sec

Time taken to finish one complete round of the track = 2 * (22/7) * 21 ÷ 11

= 12 sec

questions.q_en: If radius(R) of one circle is reduced to one fourth and radius(R) of another circle is increased to twice, then sum of the circumference of both the new circles will be_____.
questions.solution_en:
According to the question,

Let the original radius be R

Circumference of the circle = 2πR

When radius of circle is reduced to ¼, then Circumference of the circle = 2π (R/4) = πR/2

When radius of circle is increased twice, then Circumference of the circle = 2π (2R) = 4πR

Sum of the circumferences = πR/2+ 4πR = 9πR/2

questions.q_en: Find the area of triangle with sides 12 cm, 10 cm and 6 cm.
questions.solution_en:
Area of triangle = √s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)

Where s = (a + b + c)/2

According to question,

s = (12 + 10 + 6)/2 = 14 cm

Area = √(14 (14 - 12) (14 - 10)(14 - 6))

= √(14 * 2 * 4 * 8) = √896

= 8√14 cm2

questions.q_en: What is the area (in cm2) of the triangle having sides in the ratio 3: 2: 4 respectively and perimeter 36 cm?
questions.solution_en:
Perimeter = 36 cm

Then, first side = 36 * 3/9 = 12 cm

Second side = 36 * 2/9 = 8 cm

Third side = 36 * 4/9 = 16 cm

Perimeter/2 = 36/2 = 18 cm

Therefore, area = √(18 * (18 - 12) * (18 - 8) * (18 - 16))

= 12√15 cm2
